info.name: Nexus GGR — Game API + Seamless Wallet
info.description:
Integration with Nexus GGR (https://api.nexusggr.com) — slots, live casino, sportsbook, fish and mini games via a SEAMLESS wallet.

## Read this first

There are TWO directions, and confusing them is the main source of pain:

**Folder 1 — Game API.** WE call THEM. One endpoint (`{{apiEndpoint}}`), one flat JSON body, dispatched on `method`, authenticated with `agent_code` + **agent_token**.

**Folder 2 — Seamless Wallet.** THEY call US at `{{siteEndpoint}}/gold_api` on every bet and win. Authenticated with `agent_code` + **agent_secret** (a DIFFERENT value from the token). This is where real money moves.

Seamless means Nexus holds no player funds — our wallet is the source of truth, and every spin is a live HTTP call to our server.

## Two traps that cost hours

**1. Token vs Secret.** Outbound calls use `agent_token`; inbound callbacks carry `agent_secret`. Swapping them fails with `Invalid Agent`.

**2. IPv4 only.** Nexus authorises by IP, and the address registered in their panel is your IPv4 one. Verified against the live API: the identical request over IPv4 returns SUCCESS, over IPv6 returns `INVALID_IP`. If a call fails with INVALID_IP from a machine you know is whitelisted, you are egressing over IPv6. (Our backend client forces `family: 4` for this reason.)

## Saved responses

Every example in this collection was captured from the LIVE API on 2026-08-12 with the real agent account, not copied from the docs. Where the docs and reality disagree, the saved response is the truth — see 1.2, where games carry no `type` field despite the docs implying otherwise.

---

## SPORTSBOOK — Nexus back-office setup (do this in THEIR panel)

The sportsbook needs configuration in the Nexus admin panel (Profile → Sportsbook Configuration), NOT in our code. These fields tell the sportsbook iframe how to hand control back to our site when it needs to.

| Field | Set it to | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Login URL | `https://winx-88.com/login`  OR  `sendPostMessage` | Where the iframe sends a logged-OUT visitor who taps a bet. A real URL redirects there; `sendPostMessage` instead posts a browser message to your page so your own login modal opens (needs a frontend listener). |
| Deposit URL | `https://winx-88.com/deposit`  OR  `sendPostMessage` | Same idea, for a player with insufficient balance who taps Place Bet. |
| Theme | Dark | Cosmetic. Match your site. |
| Cashout RTP (%) | 92 (their default) | The return applied when a player cashes out a bet before the event settles — 92 means a 100 fair value is offered at 92. Lower = more house margin on early cashouts. |
| Min / Max Stake | 5 / 1000 | Per-bet limits, in whole BDT. |
| Default Stake Amounts | 5,25,50,100 | The quick-stake chips in the bet slip. |

**Which to choose for Login/Deposit URL.** Because a player is ALREADY logged into your site before they can open the sportsbook, `sendPostMessage` is the cleaner option — the iframe messages your page ("needs deposit") and your existing deposit modal opens, with no full-page redirect. But it requires the frontend to add a `window.addEventListener("message", ...)` handler. If that listener is not built, use the real `/login` and `/deposit` URLs so the flow at least works by redirect.

**Nothing about sportsbook BETS changes on our side.** They arrive as `game_type: "SB"` on the same `/gold_api` callback (folder 2.4), already handled and tested. The only new pieces are launching the lobby (folder 3.6) and this panel config.

item.name: 1. Game API — we call Nexus
item.description:
Outbound. Every request is `POST {{apiEndpoint}}` with a flat JSON body; `method` selects the operation. Auth is `agent_code` + `agent_token`.

Ordered as their documentation lists them.

request.description:
Start here. Also the fastest connectivity/credentials check.

**The `type` field on each provider is the authority for categorising its games** — the game list itself carries no type. Values seen on this account: `slot`, `live`, `SB`, `MN` (mini/instant), `FH` (fish hunter).

Note `FH` exists on the account but is absent from their written docs. Any integration that only handles slot/live/SB/MN will reject every fish-game bet.

response.name: 200 — 25 providers (live capture)
0 — INVALID_IP (you are on IPv6)
0 — Invalid Agent (wrong agent_code)

request.description:
Games for ONE provider. PRAGMATIC alone returns 614.

**Games carry NO `type` field** — only `id`, `game_code`, `game_name`, `banner`, `status`. Their category must be taken from the PROVIDER's type in 1.1. Deriving it from the game (e.g. by name) files every slot as a live game.

`status: 1` means playable. Skip anything else rather than listing a game that will not launch.

response.name: 200 — 614 Pragmatic games (live capture)

request.description:
Returns a playable URL to put in an iframe or redirect to.

**`user_code` MUST be our `users.username`.** It is the identity Nexus echoes back on every /gold_api callback, and our handler resolves the wallet by that username. Send anything else and bets arrive for a player we cannot find. The user is auto-created on Nexus's side at first launch — no separate registration call.

`game_code` is optional for LIVE providers; omit it to get a lobby URL instead of a specific table.

`rtp` is optional and uses the account default when omitted.

`money_info` covers both: omit `user_code` for the agent balance alone, include it to get the user block too.

**`agent.balance` is your credit float with Nexus** — worth monitoring, since running dry is a "games stop working" event rather than a gradual degradation.

**`user.balance` is ALWAYS 0 in seamless mode**, and that is correct. Nexus holds no player funds; our `wallets` table is the source of truth. Do not treat this as the player's balance.

response.name: 200 — agent + user (live capture, note user balance 0)

request.description:
Nexus's own record of rounds — the authority when reconciling a dispute against our `nexus_transactions` table.

`game_type` names the array in the response (`slot`, `live`, `SB`, `MN`, `FH`), exactly like the callback payload.

`page` is ZERO-indexed. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`.

The `user_start_balance` / `user_end_balance` fields are what Nexus believes our wallet did. If they disagree with `nexus_transactions.balance_before/after`, something is wrong on one side — this is the first place to look.

response.name: 200 — with rounds (shape from Nexus docs)

request.description:
Returns a URL to the provider's own round-replay screen — useful when a player disputes a result.

**PRAGMATIC only.** Every other provider returns `Invalid Provider`, confirmed live. Do not surface this button for non-Pragmatic games.

item.name: 2. Seamless Wallet — Nexus calls US
item.description:
Inbound. Nexus POSTs to `{{siteEndpoint}}/gold_api` on every balance check, bet and win. Auth is `agent_code` + **agent_secret** in the BODY (not a header, and not the token).

You do not run these in production — they are here to simulate Nexus and prove the endpoint behaves before real money flows.

**Every response is HTTP 200**, success or failure. A 4xx/5xx makes Nexus mark the call failed and retry — after we may already have moved the money.

Set `siteEndpoint` to your deployed host. Nexus appends `/gold_api` itself, so the value in their panel must NOT include it.

request.description:
Called when a game opens and periodically during play. Returns the player's REAL wallet balance from our database.

Note `agent_secret` here, not `agent_token`.

response.name: 200 — wrong agent_secret (still HTTP 200)

request.description:
A bet. Money leaves the player's wallet.

**The bet lives under a key NAMED BY `game_type`** — `slot`, `live`, `SB`, `MN` or `FH`. That dynamic key is why our handler takes the body untyped: a DTO with `whitelist: true` would strip it and we would process an empty transaction.

`txn_type` is `debit` | `credit` | `debit_credit`.

Amounts are WHOLE BDT, not paisa — confirmed by the sportsbook stake config (min 5, max 1000, defaults 5/25/50/100).

response.name: 200 — REPLAY of the same txn_id (idempotent)

request.description:
One call carrying both legs of a winning spin. The wallet moves ONCE by the net difference (+150 here), not twice.

Turnover still counts the STAKE only (100), never the payout.

item.name: 2.4 transaction — sportsbook (SB) and other game types

request.description:
The same handler covers all five game types — swap `game_type` and rename the nested key to match:

| game_type | nested key | shows in history as |
|---|---|---|
| `slot` | `slot` | SLOT |
| `live` | `live` | LIVE |
| `SB` | `SB` | SPORTS |
| `MN` | `MN` | CRASH |
| `FH` | `FH` | FISHING |

`FH` is absent from Nexus's written docs but present on the account — handle it or every fish-game bet fails.

SB and MN bets are accepted even though we do not currently LIST those games, so enabling them later needs no backend change.

response.name: 200 — INVALID_REQUEST (game_type with no matching object)

item.name: 3. FRONTEND — what your app calls
item.description:
**FOR THE FRONTEND DEVELOPER. Start here — ignore folders 1 and 2.**

Your app never talks to Nexus. It calls YOUR backend, which calls Nexus:

```
Browser  →  safurion.online  →  api.nexusggr.com
            (your backend)      (Nexus)
```

Folder 1 is your BACKEND calling Nexus — reference only, never called from a browser (the agent token would be exposed, and Nexus only accepts whitelisted server IPs anyway). Folder 2 is Nexus calling your backend.

## The good news: there is nothing new to build

Nexus games were deliberately added to the SAME `casino_games` table the existing Palace and OroPlay games live in. So the endpoints below are the ones you already use — Nexus games simply appear in the results, tagged by provider. No new list endpoint, no new launch call, no special-casing.

If your game list and launch already work, Nexus works the moment the backend is deployed and the catalog is synced.

query.description: slots | live | roulette | baccarat | blackjack | table | instant | fishing. Use 'live' for the whole live-casino tab.

request.description:
**No auth required.** The existing game list — Nexus games are already in it.

After a catalog sync this returns ~3300 additional games across these types:

| type | count | source |
|---|---|---|
| `slots` | 3070 | 21 Nexus slot providers |
| `blackjack` | 131 | PP Live |
| `baccarat` | 44 | PP Live |
| `roulette` | 27 | PP Live |
| `live` | 10 | PP Live |
| `instant` | 9 | Spribe |
| `fishing` | 9 | FishHunter |

Nothing in the response shape changed. Use `uuid` from each game to launch it in 3.2 — Nexus ones look like `NEXUS_PRAGMATIC_vs243mwarrior`, but you should treat it as an opaque string rather than parsing it.

response.name: 200 — list including a Nexus game

item.name: 3.2 Launch a game (works for ALL providers)

request.description:
**The endpoint you already use. No change needed.**

Pass the `uuid` from the game list; the backend works out which provider it belongs to and calls the right one — Nexus, Palace or OroPlay. Your code does not need to know the difference.

Put the returned `url` in an iframe or redirect to it.

Requires the player's JWT: the backend sends their `username` to Nexus as the player identity, and every subsequent bet callback is resolved by it.

If this returns `{}` or null, the provider rejected the launch — check the backend logs rather than retrying.

response.name: 200 — Nexus game launch (live capture)

request.description: Distinct live-casino provider names, for the provider filter chips. Nexus's live provider appears here automatically once synced.

Unchanged. Nexus bets move this balance in real time via the seamless callbacks, so refresh it after a game session.

The backend also pushes a `wallet:balance` websocket event to the player's room after every Nexus bet, so a live-updating balance needs no polling.

query.description: SLOT | LIVE | SPORTS | CRASH | FISHING | LOTTERY | JACKPOT. Omit for all.

request.description:
Existing endpoint. Nexus rounds are unioned in alongside Palace, OroPlay, sportsbook and in-house games, grouped by round.

Nexus's game types map onto the categories you already use, so no new category chips are needed:

| Nexus game_type | category shown |
|---|---|
| `slot` | SLOT |
| `live` | LIVE |
| `SB` | SPORTS |
| `MN` | CRASH |
| `FH` | FISHING |

response.name: 200 — Nexus rounds in the feed (live capture)

item.name: 3.6 Launch SPORTSBOOK (a lobby, not a tile)

request.description:
The sportsbook is ONE lobby, not a grid of games — it does not appear in /sports/games and has no uuid. Surface it as a dedicated "Sports" nav button that calls this, then open the returned url in an iframe or new tab.

Bets settle through the same seamless callback as slots (game_type "SB"), so nothing else is needed on the bet side.

REQUIRES the Nexus back-office sportsbook setup (see the collection description) — Login URL and Deposit URL must be configured there, or a logged-out / underfunded player hits a dead end inside the iframe.

response.name: 200 — sportsbook lobby URL

item.name: 4. Admin routes (backoffice)
item.description: WinX88's own endpoints for managing the Nexus catalog. Admin JWT, not Nexus credentials.

request.description: Proxies 1.1 through our backend. The fastest way to confirm the server can reach Nexus and that its IP is whitelisted — an `INVALID_IP` here means the SERVER's address is not registered, regardless of whether your laptop works.

Walks every provider and upserts their games into `casino_games` with `aggregator='NEXUS'`. Safe to re-run — it upserts rather than deleting, so a partial failure never empties the catalog.

Pass `{"providerCode":"PRAGMATIC"}` to sync one provider only.

Takes a few minutes for the full catalog.

response.name: 200 — full sync (live capture)

request.description: Counts by provider and type — confirms games landed in the right tabs after a sync.

Player-facing launch. The existing `/sports/games/:uuid?searchType=real` route also works and routes Nexus games here automatically, so the frontend needs no change.

The player's `username` is sent as `user_code`, which is what ties the launch to the wallet callbacks.
